description: Proving who the caller is with a password, a one-time code or a token from a trusted issuer.
Deciding what an authenticated caller may do, by comparing its roles or permissions with the requested action.
401 means the caller is not authenticated, 403 means the caller is known but not allowed.
The line where data enters from outside, such as a request, and must be treated as hostile.
A new endpoint stays closed until a rule opens it on purpose, so a forgotten rule fails safe.
Each role or token receives only the permissions its tasks require.
A deliberately slow, salted hash such as bcrypt that makes guessing stored passwords expensive.
